geometry_and_admissibility: For real n, set x=n³,y=(n+1)³,a=log x,b=log y,H=b−a,h=HK/(K+1),δ=H/(K+1). Let g=1_[a,a+h]∗δ⁻¹1_[0,δ]. Then 0≤g≤1, support⊆[a,b], g(a)=g(b)=0, ∫g=h.

Convolve with a nonnegative smooth unit-mass compact mollifier to obtain gε. Wε(t)=√(x/(2t))gε(log(2t)), X=2, is smooth with compact support in [1,∞) when ε is small, since x>2. This meets every hypothesis of the actual general SourceGreenSmooth; no source formula for a nonsmooth weight is postulated.

Its source Mellin packet is √x∫gε(w)e^((s−1/2)w)dw. The pole tends to at least xh. At ρ=1/2+iγ its modulus is at most √x h |sinc(γh/2)sinc(γδ/2)|, with sinc u=sin u/u. For T=2/h this is √x h f_K(γ/T). This is the radian sinc convention used by the actual πj/M grid.

Mollifier transforms have modulus≤1. f_K(u)≤min(1,K/u²), BPT counting gives an absolutely summable zero majorant; trivial zeros have a convergent geometric majorant. Thus dominated limits justify unsmoothing. The Λ sum is finite locally and converges termwise, and endpoint weights tend to zero. The resulting prime window is strictly open.

RH puts nontrivial zeros on the critical line. Both signs contribute factor2 and integer order multiplicities are retained. Real zeros in (0,1) are excluded by ζ(σ)=η(σ)/(1−2^(1−σ))<0: η(σ)>0 by paired alternating terms. This written argument removes Nicolas; the old Lean order_zero_on_real_axis lemma itself still requires Nicolas, so its type is not silently changed.
zero_enclosure: T=2/h≥2n/3; low interval up to Tπj0/M plus finite (Tπj/M,Tπ(j+1)/M] cells and >TπJ/M tail cover all positive zeros including jump heights. j0=21 or31 makes every sampled height exceed2π.

Each cell sinc upper uses exact Taylor9 sine enclosures with angle folding, Lipschitz allowances π_hi/(2M) and π_hi/(2MK), positive denominator u_lower, clamp at1 and upward 10^−10 rounding. Low f≤1 and tail K/u² are conservative.
Integration against the smooth BPT main term uses 2hT=4 exactly; low and cell weights2j0/M and2m_j/M, tail2K/(πuJ)[logT+log(J/(2M))+1]. The 7/8 term is bounded by21/(4n).
Discrete residual summation uses total variation |1−m_j0|+Σ|Δm|+m_last+3K/uJ². The tail residual≤.28(K/uJ²)(2log(TuJ)+.5) is absorbed since log(TuJ)≥.5; with2h≤6/n the residual cap is(42/25)(L+C)V/n.

logT≤L−.37 orL−.4. Rounding A upward while B upward remains safe despite the negative offset, because L+offset>0. Independent assembly checks the exact coupled budget rather than testing only rounded scalars.
prime_powers_continuum_and_seam: Square bases: at most1.5√(n+1)+1 and logp≤1.5log(n+1). For exponents m≥3 each root interval has length≤1, hence at most2 integer bases per exponent and <5log(n+1) exponents. The normalized loss is≤2L/n^(3/2)+4L²/n². This elementary bound consumes no Nicolas input.

Trivial-zero normalized loss≤1/(3n^5). Main normalized lower≥[K/(K+1)]·[n/(n+1)]/[1+1/(nL)]. Main increases; zero cap decreases on the whole ray by A(log n−2)+B≥0, and power/trivial losses decrease. Thus the continuum ray is proved by monotonicity, not sampled n values.
K32/M64/J16384 yields coefficient>.8591 for every real n≥exp8. K480/M96/J196608 yields>.9855 for every real n≥2154433.
